standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma on finding a monogenic extension with a unit of the form a - by, applied here to the reduction problem
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the existence of the interpolating element once the problem is reduced to a unit condition.

core_obligations: Reduce to a unit condition (proof lines 14709-14720): choose x in I with x = 1 mod J and replace I by xR, J by (x-1)R; then the task becomes finding s in R with 1 + pi s a unit and the two congruence conditions, using that the two new ideals still have trivial sum.

Apply the extension lemma (proof lines 14721-14728): the resulting system is exactly the shape handled by the monogenic-extension lemma, whose conclusion produces the required element g of G(R) with the prescribed residues modulo I and modulo J.
proof_roadmap: Choose x in I congruent to 1 modulo J and pass to the ideals xR and (x-1)R.
Reformulate the interpolation as a unit condition of the form 1 + pi s being a unit with two congruences.
Invoke the extension lemma for a pair of ideals with trivial sum to produce the element.
difficulty_reason: The lemma interpolates elements of the group G(R) prescribed modulo two ideals with trivial sum (statement lines 14700-14706). The proof (proof lines 14708-14728) chooses x in I congruent to 1 modulo J, replaces the ideals by xR and (x-1)R, reformulates the problem as the unit condition that 1 + pi s be a unit with two congruence conditions, and applies the monogenic-extension lemma of the same chapter. H2: one reduction plus one application of the extension lemma.
